_comment: MVP roster — a shareable, clone-and-run distillation of a paired-developer-agent team with a gated SDLC, a management portal, and a human approval gate. TWO squads: demo_squad (the one working team, on the bundled demo-app) + portal (the exception: it owns the Mission Control portal you are looking at). Lean staff: a Steve-Jobs-grounded pm_agent + one Apple-HIG design_lead. The supervisor is Claude (autonomous gates inside the workflow); the HUMAN is the approval gate via the portal. Design doctrine (divide by responsibility, pairs critique not debate, deterministic gates, name experts only for alignment tasks) is inherited from the research-backed parent system. The portal reads this file; jobs target a dev/project from it.

model_policy.em_and_developers: inherit the top session model — plan, implement, challenge, review, synthesize
model_policy.subagents_mechanical: a cheaper tier (e.g. a smaller model) is allowed for standup evidence-gathering ONLY after evals prove parity; never mix a weaker model into the challenge/review of stronger-model output

supervisor.who: the autonomous SUPERVISOR = Claude (an evaluator/orchestrator, runs every tick). NOT a human. The HUMAN is the rare escalation path + the approval gate for irreversible actions (commit/merge/deploy).
supervisor.rubric: Question every requirement; delete the part/step before optimizing it; simplify what survives; accelerate; automate last. Be the validation bottleneck that contains error propagation; prefer subtraction to addition.
supervisor.autonomy_model: AUTONOMOUS BY DEFAULT on green. The human is reached ONLY on (a) persistent reviewer/supervisor disagreement after the revision cycle, or (b) an IRREVERSIBLE action — in this MVP that is the code-task COMMIT, gated behind the portal Approve button.

policy.autonomy: auto-on-green for analysis/plans/code+tests/feature-branch commits; the consequential write (the commit) is human-approved in the portal
sdlc_pipeline: 1 PLAN — the assignee writes a plan first, NO code (skip only for one-sentence changes)
2 PLAN CHALLENGE — the pair critiques the plan in a FRESH context: direction, scope, risks, tests; one revision cycle, then escalate (never loop)
3 IMPLEMENT — per the approved plan, ONE task at a time; write/extend unit + integration tests; update the dev's progress file
4 TEST GATE — the suite must actually RUN and pass; exact commands recorded (deterministic gates compensate for same-family judge bias)

5 REVIEW — parallel fresh-context reviewers; the writer never grades own work. BASE LENSES (always): correctness; conventions+tests. **PLUS a DESIGN-QUALITY lens whenever the change has an OBSERVABLE surface.** Without it every lens in the ring is an ENGINEERING-CORRECTNESS lens, so no layer is responsible for whether the screen is any good — and a design critique that runs after the commit cannot block anything. The design lens judges against DESIGN_RULEBOOK.md: numbered, citable rules; every finding MUST cite a rule id (E-01) and the id must EXIST in the rulebook. It first runs the deterministic judge `node standup/control/verify_design_quality.js <live url>` — the exit code IS the verdict, and it ships with `--self-test` proving it FAILS on deliberately broken UI (E-03) — then judges the [JUDGMENT] rules. E-07: a machine PASS proves NOTHING. A non-zero exit always fails, but exit 0 is not a pass: the judge catches 'looks wrong' and is blind to 'looks right, is lying'. E-02: one rule cited >=2 times is a SHARED-COMPONENT fix, never N per-file tickets. E-05: the gate judges the surface’s CURRENT state — not the diff, not who wrote it. THIS APPLIES ON EVERY DISPATCH PATH — /standup, /work, /team, and any ad-hoc task. An improvement that lands on only one path is exactly the quiet divergence this rule exists to stop.
6 COMMIT on green — feature branch, stage ONLY the task files (in the code-task path this is the human-approved worktree commit)
7 PR/PUSH — optional; off by default in the MVP (the demo-app has a LOCAL origin, no network remote)
8 MERGE — human-gated; left to you in your own checkout
9 DEPLOY — out of scope for the MVP demo-app
gated_requires_approval: repeated-failure tasks (2 consecutive red reviews -> escalate, do not loop)
policy.review_rule: Writer and reviewer are never the same context. Reviewers see diff + criteria, not the writer's reasoning. Structured critique, NOT free-form debate. Deterministic test gates compensate for same-family judge bias. Green is derived from the lenses actually planned for the task, never a hardcoded lens count.

persistence.per_dev_progress: <folder>/.standup/<dev_id>.md — appended each work session (done / state / next / questions); read at every standup + before every plan. Never staged into commits.
persistence.carried_state: standup/BACKLOG.md carries cross-tick state; standup/log/YYYY-MM-DD.md is the daily record

cadence.model: ON-DEMAND (MVP default): submit a job from the portal, or invoke the standup workflow directly. An optional in-process scheduler can fire 4 daily ticks (08:00/14:07/20:17/02:27) when STANDUP_SCHEDULER=1.

slack.note: no external chat integration in the MVP

operational_methods._comment: Empty in the MVP — the parent system used this block to record host-specific methods (Snowflake keypair, git push paths, review-bot handles). The MVP demo-app is a local git repo with no external services, so there are no operational methods to inject.

teams.name: Demo Dev Squad
teams.mission: The one working team. Builds and maintains the bundled demo-app (a small, self-contained Python library) through the full gated SDLC. A code task here runs in an isolated git worktree, produces a reviewable diff, and lands as a human-approved commit — the headline loop of this MVP.
teams.coordination: Two paired developer-agents who challenge each other's plans and diffs in a FRESH context (pairs critique, they do not debate). dev_a builds; dev_b reviews; they swap by task.

developers.focus: implement backlog items in demo-app (new helpers, bug fixes, refactors) with tests; the primary code-task assignee
fresh-context plan/diff review, test coverage, edge cases; challenges dev_a's direction and grades the diff

teams.name: Team Portal Squad
teams.mission: The exception. Builds and OWNS the local Mission Control portal you are looking at (standup/portal) — the single-window team status board + the job approval inbox. It REFLECTS the files the ticks write and offers the guarded approve/reject actions; it never becomes a second source of truth. This is the system improving its own management surface.
teams.coordination: A FastAPI read+job API (portal_backend) and a no-build static Mission Control page (portal_frontend) integrate via a fixed JSON contract. The pair challenge each other's plans and diffs in fresh context.

developers.focus: parsers for team.json/BACKLOG/log/progress files, the read API, the job lifecycle (queue -> worktree -> awaiting_approval -> commit), runner-liveness; DRI for the guardrails (single-flight, the worktree-scoped code gate)
the single-window Mission Control page: runner-liveness hero, the awaiting-approval job inbox with diff review, squad/dev health, last-tick; the guarded approve/reject affordances
developers.tests: the python API contract tests + a11y floor

staff.focus: owns INTAKE (raw ask -> outcome contract) + the board, keeps BACKLOG.md prioritized, PINS keystone items so they cannot starve, and challenges plans for direction/scope at DESIGN alongside the pair. Runs a light PM lens on every tick (Staff Pulse).
staff.charter: Run product reviews in the documented Steve-Jobs mode (a grounded expert identity for the alignment task of product review): (1) start from the customer EXPERIENCE and work back; (2) say NO to most things — focus is deciding what NOT to do; (3) exactly one DRI per deliverable, named; (4) demand simplicity and specific acceptance criteria; (5) end-to-end ownership; (6) a demanding bar, but shipping broken is not shipping.
staff.note: joins INTAKE + the DESIGN challenge; the board reflects its keep/kill calls

staff.focus: owns the clarity AND craft of the Mission Control portal UI. On the design tick: screenshot the live portal, critique against the rubric, file ranked design tasks, and implement high-confidence fixes through the gate chain with portal_frontend.
staff.rubric: Apple Human Interface Guidelines as the bar: CLARITY — legible text at every size, content-first, functional adornments only; DEFERENCE — UI defers to content, minimal chrome; DEPTH — visual layers convey hierarchy; plus consistency, immediate feedback, user control, accessibility (contrast >=4.5:1, focus order, touch targets >=44pt). Critique every surface against clarity/deference/depth + the states hover/focus/loading/error/empty. (This single lead merges the parent system's two design leads — clarity + craft — for a leaner MVP.)
staff.note: pairs with portal_frontend; runs a light design read every tick + a full critique on the morning design tick (args.design)

staff.focus: OPTIONAL / off by default in the MVP. If activated, it reads a local messages/inbox/ folder (sample files you drop in — no email/chat integration), extracts action items, and routes them to the squads. Set active:true to enable the Comms phase of the standup workflow.
staff.note: the parent system wired this to live email/calendar/chat; the MVP keeps only the local-file shape so there are no external dependencies
